notes: Both configurations scored 92.9%. Not one of the 13 assertions separates the new version from the snapshot, so this iteration proves no improvement.

returning-shopper-skips-profile is compromised by its own prompt: the shopper recites their whole profile in the message, so both arms skip the questions by reading the message rather than by following the rule. It tests nothing about the 'Skip what you already know' edit. Rewrite it to supply the profile out of band before trusting 6/6.
first-trip-brief-order is a regression check by construction. The nine-question brief already existed in the snapshot, so 6/7 on both sides means nothing broke, not that anything improved.

The one shared failure is a genuine defect the eval earned: turn four asks three questions (budget, care, store) whenever the store is not already evident, which breaks the skill's own 'two questions at a time, never more' rule. Both versions do it, because Step 1's layout causes it.

The only visible behavioural difference is unmeasured. The new run states it will use the store's own menu and filters rather than guessing a category URL; the snapshot run says nothing of the kind. The assertion that would catch this lives in category-url-discipline, which did not run because it needs a live browser.

Cost moved the wrong way on case 1: 89,610 tokens and 228s for the new version against 79,488 and 140s for the snapshot. The added navigation section is the likely cause. Worth watching if SKILL.md keeps growing.
